pr_title: Make initialization of tokenizer and detokenizer optional
pr_body:
Add a flag to initialize the LLM engine to disable tokenizer. 
If tokenizer is disabled, so does detokenizer.


FIX #3635 
FIX #3647
pr_comments:
Thanks for making this PR! It appears to me that unlike https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/3749 to allow skipping detokenization at sampling param level, this PR simply disables the use of tokenizer as a whole, so I guess the two PRs can still co-exist.

We might want to be careful with all these API changes though - cc @simon-mo
@GeauxEric Thank you for the contribution! Could you update this branch with the changes merged in the main branch? Happy to review after the conflicts are resolved!

> * you can pass in `prompt_token_ids` instead of `prompt` to skip tokenization


Thanks for the feedback.
To better clarify the intent, I changed the the title to be _Make **initialization** of tokenizer and detokenizer optional_ from _Make tokenization and detokenization optional_

As found in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/3647, the code always tries to initialize tokenizer, even its API intends to make it optional.

In addition to the performance overhead, there are other concerning factors about the actual development, production and architecture.

1. Every user needs to prepare a vocab file to initialize tokenizer, even it is not used during the runtime. The engineering time wasted scales  with the number engineers who do not need tokenization. 
2. The build size is much larger, as the vocab file needs to be included; the size of the vocab is huge these days.
3. The tokenizer/de-tok is pinned to Huggingface class and methods, forbidding users from using their own implementations, or separate tok/de-tok as micro-services.

If this make sense, I will continue to resolve the comments.

I think it's reasonable to not require a tokenizer. However, as @ywang96 alluded to vLLM currently assumes there is an `eos_token_id` and that it comes from the tokenizer. It's used in stopping evaluation and min_tokens logic. So we either need to also make eos token optional and handle that in those places, or require an explicit eos token id to be configured in the case that no tokenizer is configured.

> 3. The tokenizer/de-tok is pinned to Huggingface class and methods, forbidding users from using their own implementations, or separate tok/de-tok as micro-services.

As @ywang96 said, the last part of this isn't really true, since `prompt_token_ids` along with `detokenize=False` can be used in requests to allow tok/de-tok to be handled in another layer.

> urrently assumes there is an eos_token_id and that it comes from the tokenizer. It's used in stopping evaluation and min_tokens logic. So we either need to also make eos token optional and handle that in those places, or require an explicit eos token id to be configured in the case that no tokenizer is configured.

Thanks. I will move on to make the change. 
Making this PR in draft mode for now to avoid spam people.

> So we either need to also make eos token optional and handle that in those places, or require an explicit eos token id to be configured in the case that no tokenizer is configured.

This is not needed, because user can provide the eos token ids in the sampling parameter.

> > So we either need to also make eos token optional and handle that in those places, or require an explicit eos token id to be configured in the case that no tokenizer is configured.
> 
> This is not needed, because user can provide the eos token ids in the sampling parameter.

True, but it would be to retain the existing behaviour of stopping at EOS by default. Agree though that it's probably fine to not have this.
Maybe others can help take a look? @simon-mo?
Could you please take another look and consider merging/approving it when you have a moment?

issue_context.title: [Feature]: make _init_tokenizer optional and support initiate LLMEngine without tokenizer
issue_context.body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

Currently the `generate` method supports inference based on `prompt_token_ids`:
```
    def generate(
        self,
        prompts: Optional[Union[str, List[str]]] = None,
        sampling_params: Optional[SamplingParams] = None,
        prompt_token_ids: Optional[List[List[int]]] = None,
        use_tqdm: bool = True,
        lora_request: Optional[LoRARequest] = None,
    ) -> List[RequestOutput]:
```
that means tokenizer is optional to the LLM engine. 

However, to initiate an LLM engine, it always calls  [`_init_tokenizer` ](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/engine/llm_engine.py#L167), which effectively makes tokenizer required.

The LLM engine cannot be initialized without a valid tokenizer argument. 

In our application, we would love to use LLM's powerful engine for inference, but want to keep tokenizer as a separate service.

### Alternatives

_No response_

### Additional context
